newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates up, but Issing remarks may help.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates up, but Issing remarks may help.

text.p: Dutch money dealers said Friday's remarks by Bundesbank official Otmar Issing lessened pain in the market, since his Wednesday comments about the possible direction of German interest rates had put upward pressure on guilder deposits.
Issing said that "under existing circumstances," there would be no rate cut in Germany, but he did not completely rule out a trimming in official rates in the future.
"It is a relief for the market," said one dealer, adding the signals had been confusing.
On Wednesday Issing said key rates were at a historic low and nothing more was to be expected, which quashed rate cut hopes in the market.

Dealers said rates had been edging up in the past few days, but it was likely that had come to an end now. "Technically speaking there is no reason for the higher rates at the moment," said one dealer.
Today's allocation of 3.71 billion guilders under a six-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent was ample, dealers said.
Market players added the Dutch state was still searching for liquidity and was bringing Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) into the market.
"This keeps rates a bit higher as well," said one dealer.
Call rates were trading at 2.81 percent bid, unchanged from Thursday.
Three-month deposits rose two basis points to 2.86 percent bid and one-year paper added four basis points to 3.08 percent.
"But the upward pressure is fading," said one dealer.
The guilder gained against the mark to 112.155 per 100 marks from 112.17 on Thursday.
